kjv: the company of the Ashurites have made thy (Tyre's) benches [of] ivory
mine: they made your (Tyre's) deck of ivory inlaid in cypress
note: bat-ashurim is best read as one word bit'ashurim "in cypress (te'ashur) wood"; KJV split it into "daughter/company of the Ashurites", inventing an Assyrian guild of craftsmen.
nofekh and kadkod are uncertain gemstones; nofekh is probably turquoise (or garnet), and kadkod a red stone such as ruby; KJV's identifications are guesses.
occupy here meant "trade" and "fairs" render izbonim "wares/goods", not markets or festivals; modern readers miss the commercial sense.
me'uzzal is "from Uzal" (a place in Arabia, Gen 10:27), not the participle "going to and fro".
